title: Act III, Scene I
focus: 'To be, or not to be' and the nunnery scene

teacherSummary.text: Rosencrantz and Guildenstern report failure. Claudius and Polonius hide to watch Hamlet with Ophelia. Hamlet meditates on life, death and action. Ophelia returns his gifts; he denies loving her, tells her to go to a nunnery, and rails against marriage. Claudius decides to send Hamlet to England.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “To be, or not to be: that is the question” slowly and put it in my own words: Alone, Hamlet asks whether it is better to exist or not to exist. Next, craft. I notice the stark, balanced opening, two short infinitives set against each other. The strongest word is “question”: it frames life itself as a problem to be reasoned through. Then, effect. What question is Hamlet weighing in this soliloquy? My answer: Hamlet weighs whether enduring life's pain is better than ending it, and concludes that fear of what comes after death makes people suffer on; the speech shows how thought paralyzes his action.

criticalVoices.quote: Hence we see a great, an almost enormous, intellectual activity, and a proportionate aversion to real action consequent upon it, with all its symptoms and accompanying qualities.
